M1.evidence: The transaction takes ExplorationRepository.lock_command_key before _replay, candidate UUID/time construction and append. Its user/project/actor_scope=user_id/APPEND_REVISION/command_id scope exactly matches the existing M8 append guard because candidate.created_by=user_id. PostgreSQL advisory transaction-lock acquisition therefore serializes same-command callers; the later repository acquisition is reentrant in the same transaction. After the first caller commits, the waiter reads the receipt and reconstructs the stored revision rather than generating a competing identity. Replay now requires candidate_id=None for genesis, the exact recorded candidate id for updates, and the corresponding expected version. Both previously accepted shape changes are rejected. Changed draft/actor/author class still rebuild to a different payload and conflict. The new PG route tests cover simultaneous identical calls returning equal 200 responses and genesis reshaping refusal.
M1.probe: A deterministic in-memory transaction-lock model executed the real append/replay/build functions with real contracts. Two identical concurrent calls produced one repository append and equal responses. Genesis-to-explicit-update and update-to-omitted-candidate changes each raised CommandReplayConflictError. The fake repository models command ownership and receipt visibility; this is not an observed PG interleaving.
M1.run_id_equivalence_judgment: ACCEPTED by construction. PackagingCandidate binds assessed subject, master and profile/constraints/closures, not a unique quality_run_id. For the same verified subject/profile and identical authored input/provenance, two runs yield the same candidate payload and M8 lineage. An actual build_payload probe confirmed equality when only run_id changed. Treating this lookup identity as necessarily distinct command intent in the prior review was stronger than the implemented domain contract requires. Packaging checks and previews independently bind exact quality_run_id and quality_run_digest, and selection/export revalidate that bound run; append replay cannot replace that later authority. Different derived subject/profile/content/provenance still conflicts. No run-ID-specific receipt/schema expansion is required to close this finding.
M1.limits: Run/profile lookup still precedes the command guard and replay. These are immutable historical reads and take no opposing writer locks here; this is not a fresh demonstrated failure. No unsupported SQLite concurrency guarantee is inferred from the PG-only advisory helper.

N1.evidence: The source is owned by os.fdopen before work.create(DOWNLOAD_FILE). An exception creating the target unwinds the source context; errors after target creation also close target. The regression injects ENOSPC after opening a real archive and checks the process fd count is unchanged. The complete plan suite passed independently: 11 tests. A separate injected-ENOSPC function probe verified the acquired source descriptor raises EBADF afterwards. The failed target-create path no longer leaks that source fd.

N2.status: FIXED for the reported response cleanup defect
N2.evidence: _ClosingStream wraps the complete StreamingResponse ASGI call in try/finally and dispatches Download.close there, so cleanup is no longer a trailing BackgroundTask skipped by a stream exception. This also covers an exception before chunk iteration. Download.close marks itself closed before releasing snapshot/work/store, so a later sequential close cannot close recycled descriptor numbers. The new tests assert one close on normal completion, send OSError and RuntimeError. A real-fd probe called Download.close twice and verified both fds were closed with one work.close. Bounded _ClosingStream probes confirmed its finally runs once for completion, OSError, RuntimeError and CancelledError.
N2.limits: The focused stream pytest run did not complete locally (45-second timeout); no threaded runtime pass is claimed. The response probes used async content and replaced loop.run_in_executor with an immediately completed future, keeping the actual _ClosingStream and asyncio.to_thread control flow but deliberately removing worker-thread scheduling. They prove ownership/control flow, not real-executor cancellation races. The builder-reported PG route result exercises successful HTTP streaming but is supplied evidence, not a reviewer execution.
